done.why: Every way forward I found was closed with 'will have to wait': three carousel passages, the ledge at the Deep Ford, the stream east of it. The barrow door is sealed. I'd covered the whole loop of rooms twice. The unicorn's key wasn't mine to take, and filling the teapot or pouring it on the roses did nothing. I had nothing left to go after.

about: You're shut inside a barrow and go down into a dim cavern under the Great Underground Empire. Past it are a disorienting spinning room, a formal garden with a gazebo, and a unicorn wearing a gold key that's meant for somebody else. A wizard flickers in and out. It feels like the first chapter of something bigger: the place keeps telling you that what lies beyond will have to wait.

moments.note: The sword starts glowing blue as I come into the garden. It's a good warning that something is close.
The carousel room sends me somewhere other than the way I picked. It's disorienting, as it promised.
The unicorn's ribbon is 'tied in the sort of bow meant to be untied by somebody in particular'. A clear goal with a lovely hook.
North from the north end of the garden took me to the Dark Tunnel. It was hard to fit the map together.
Northeast from the Great Cavern came out on the Foot Bridge, which is north of it. The geography is odd.
The place mat is described as thin enough to slide under a door. A hint I filed away hopefully.
The wizard appeared, muttered into his beard and vanished.
I poured the teapot water on the roses and it just evaporated. The message also printed twice.
The ledge gives way again. Every frontier is gated, and I had nothing left to try.

wished: Get the unicorn's gold key, or find out who the 'somebody in particular' is
Find a door to slide the place mat under
Get past the rockfalls in the carousel room or along the ledge at the Deep Ford
Have some use for the teapot of water
Take everything off the tea table with one command

lines.line: The ribbon is tied in the sort of bow that is meant to be untied by somebody in particular, and the unicorn's look makes it plain that you are not the somebody.
lines.why: It set a goal and teased me at the same time. This was the hook I most wanted to follow.

lines.line: thin enough to slide under most doors, should you ever need to slide something under a door.
lines.why: A wink of a hint that made me want to find the door.

lines.line: The way up has gone, for now. Whatever is along there will have to wait.
lines.why: It told me plainly that this was the edge of what's here, so I stopped hunting.

lines.line: you could walk past it without knowing it was a door, which, from this side, is rather the point.

fun.why: The sword glow, the unicorn and the wizard made the opening feel alive. But nothing I tried solved anything, and the second half was walking back and forth through closed edges.

engagement.why: The unicorn's key and the place mat hint gave me goals early. Interest faded once every lead ran into a rockfall or did nothing.

difficulty.why: There was little to solve. Getting around was easy apart from the carousel, which was a mild bit of chaos. The challenge was mostly working out that there was no more.

interestingness.why: Good seeds: a key you can't take, a doorless mat, a lidless teapot, a wizard. None of them came to anything in this stretch.

prose.why: The added descriptions are witty and specific: the roses 'that have been talked to', the hedges, the barrow door, the unicorn's bow.
